description: ACSIMSEP is Paul Hines and the University of Vermont's quasi-steady-state simulator of cascading failures in large electric transmission systems. It applies an AC formulation to the evolution of network separation and supplies compiled test programs. Inputs are transmission-system cases and disturbance assumptions; outputs are simulated cascade and power-system responses. The repository establishes no fixed country, historical period or universal time step, since these depend on the study case. Source is free under GPL-3.0, with build instructions for SuiteSparse and Coin-Bonmin dependencies. A limitation is sparse user documentation: the README mainly describes compilation and acknowledges that further documentation is still absent. Reuse therefore requires familiarity with the supplied test programs and the quasi-steady-state assumptions. ACSIMSEP can support cascading-failure research on infrastructure networks. DCSIMSEP (model-dcsimsep) provides a related DC approximation. No code was compiled and no model archive or input case was downloaded.
name: ACSIMSEP AC cascading-failure simulator
notes: G7 G7-1009. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-28; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability.
